title: Rust test suite leaks a temp directory per test (termal-test-state-* never removed)
outcome:
MEASURED 2026-08-26 on Greg's machine: 11,714 termal-* entries / 434 MB in %TEMP%, ALL created since 10:30 today (one day of test runs). Breakdown: 10,351 termal-test-state-* dirs, 418 termal-telegram-project-*, 363 termal-orchestrators-test-*.json, 66 termal-delegation-state-*, 66 termal-board-routes-*, 11 each of termal-codex-home-legacy/-limited, termal-summary-*, termal-telegram-*-mirror-home. 10,351 / 802 call sites is roughly 13 full-suite runs. Of a 400-dir sample of termal-test-state-*, 155 hold a termal.sqlite (avg 76 KB, written by the synchronous persist fallback) and 20 a coordination.sqlite (100 KB); 245 are empty - so the cost is inodes AND bytes.

ROOT CAUSE. test_app_state() (src/tests/mod.rs:683) and test_app_state_with_live_persist_channel() (src/tests/persist.rs:1793) create std::env::temp_dir()/termal-test-state-<uuid> plus an orchestrator_templates_path termal-orchestrators-test-<uuid>.json and hand them to AppState with NO OWNER: no Drop guard, no explicit removal anywhere, and AppState (src/state.rs:827, #[derive(Clone)]) has no Drop. 802 call sites; 213 state.clone() sites in tests; nothing ever deletes the directory. This is the 88 percent case.

SECONDARY LEAKERS (same shape, no cleanup at all): create_telegram_settings_project_and_session (src/tests/telegram_support.rs:409) creates a project root per call; temp_delegation_state_paths (src/tests/delegation_support.rs:68-71) creates two roots per call.

WHY EVEN 'CLEANED' SITES LEAK ON WINDOWS. (a) cleanup-after-assert: e.g. src/tests/codex_discovery.rs opens rusqlite::Connection at :75 and calls let _ = fs::remove_dir_all at :114 while that connection is still in scope - on Windows the open handle locks state_5.sqlite, removal fails, and let _ swallows it; any assert panic before :114 leaks too. That file is 13 temp_dir sites to 13 remove_dir_all and still leaks 11 dirs per run. (b) Guard-vs-handle lifetime: BoardRouteTempRoot (coordination_board_routes.rs:465) is a proper Drop guard, yet 66 termal-board-routes-* leak per day - consistent with an AppState clone (110 thread::spawn sites in tests) still holding the Arc<CoordinationBoardStore> connection when the guard drops.

FOUR PRIVATE DUPLICATE GUARDS already exist and should become one: TempDirCleanup (src/tests/agent_commands.rs:16), TempStateDir (src/state_accessors.rs:189), MailboxTestRoot (src/mailboxes_store_tests.rs:25), BoardRouteTempRoot (src/tests/coordination_board_routes.rs:465). No tempfile dev-dependency; no cleanup script in the repo.

FIX (test infrastructure only; no production behavior change):
F1. One shared TestTempRoot guard in src/tests/mod.rs: creates the dir, Drop calls remove_dir_all, and on failure prints the path and error to stderr instead of let _ - a leak must be visible, not silent.
F2. Give AppState ownership in tests with minimal churn: a #[cfg(test)] test_temp_root: Option<Arc<TestTempRoot>> field declared LAST in the struct (Rust drops fields in declaration order, so sqlite/board connections close before the guard runs). test_app_state() and the live-persist variant populate it; production code never sees it. Because AppState is Clone, the directory goes away when the LAST clone drops - clones parked in never-ending threads would still retain their dir, but that is the exception rather than 100 percent. (Alternative - returning the guard from test_app_state - touches all 802 call sites; not recommended.)
F3. Extra paths register on the same guard (cfg(test) state.register_test_temp_path(path)): the orchestrator templates json, telegram project roots, delegation roots.
F4. Convert cleanup-after-assert sites (codex_discovery.rs, acp_gemini.rs and similar) to a guard declared BEFORE any handle is opened, so panics and Windows locks cannot leak.
F5. Replace the four private guards with the shared one.
F6. Optional hygiene: scripts/clean-test-temp.ps1 and .sh removing termal-* entries older than 1 hour, for machines that already accumulated debris.

ACCEPTANCE: run the full cargo test --bin termal, then Get-ChildItem :TEMP -Filter 'termal-*' | Measure-Object must report at most a handful of entries (only states retained by never-ending test threads), and the guard must print every path it failed to remove so any remainder is diagnosable. Run twice back to back on Windows to catch handle-lock ordering.

IMMEDIATE RELIEF (manual, when no cargo test is running): Get-ChildItem :TEMP -Filter 'termal-*' -Force | Remove-Item -Recurse -Force
disposal_reason: Already delivered by the completed successor w-36ed6aab3dc0: independent evaluation ef0fc642 passed 4/4 (note 4fb44624); commit 3381d277 is an ancestor of master 1495e8d3. src/state.rs:1204 gives AppState last-field Arc<TestTempRoot> ownership, which removes the per-test termal-test-state-* leak. The old leak measurements and provenance are retained on this item.
